questions.q: Butanamide is warmed with Br₂ and aqueous NaOH. The organic product is:
questions.explain: Hofmann bromamide degradation is a step-down reaction: the C=O carbon leaves as CO₂ (trapped as Na₂CO₃), so the amine has one carbon fewer than the amide.

questions.q: Which intermediate is formed when the alkyl group migrates from carbon to nitrogen in the Hofmann bromamide degradation?
questions.explain: R shifts to nitrogen as Br⁻ leaves the N-bromoamide anion, in one step, giving the isocyanate; this is then hydrolysed to a carbamic acid that loses CO₂. No free nitrene forms in the accepted mechanism.

questions.q: Which amide does NOT give an amine with Br₂/NaOH?
questions.explain: Only primary amides (–CONH₂) react, because the nitrogen must lose two hydrogens during N-bromination and deprotonation. N-Methylacetamide has only one N–H. Benzamide works and gives aniline.

questions.q: Acetamide is treated with Br₂ and a base in methanol as the solvent, instead of water. The main product is:
questions.explain: Methanol is a nucleophilic solvent and traps the methyl isocyanate as a carbamate before it can be hydrolysed and decarboxylated to the amine.
